PIR - Azure Virtual Machines Scale Sets and VM Management Operation Errors in East US
What happened? Between 17:43 UTC and 22:40 UTC on 26 Jun 2026, a platform issue resulted in an impact to the Virtual Machine Scale Sets and Virtual Machine service in the East US. Impacted customers experienced error notifications when performing service management operations - such as create, delete, update, restart, reimage, start, scale, stop - for resources hosted in this region What went wrong, and why? We determined that Virtual Machines and Virtual Machine Scale Sets management operations in the East US region experienced failures due to an uneven distribution of service resources, which led to increased utilization and delays in request processing. This condition occurred during platform upgrade activities, which temporarily impacted how workloads were distributed, causing some resources to become overloaded. As a result, this led to intermittent request failures and increased response times for management operations. How did we respond? 17:43 UTC on 26 June 2026 – Customer impact began, with intermittent failures observed in Virtual Machine Scale Set management operations in the East US region.18:00 UTC on 26 June 2026 – Automated service monitoring detected an increase in failed requests and a drop in success rates.18:05 UTC on 26 June 2026 – Investigation identified uneven distribution of service resources, resulting in increased utilization and delays in request processing during ongoing update activities.18:10 UTC on 26 June 2026 – Mitigation workstream was initiated, including pausing update activities to prevent further resource imbalance and starting workload rebalancing efforts.19:00 UTC on 26 June 2026 - Additional corrective actions were taken, including targeted redistribution of workloads and controlled restarts of select service components to reduce pressure and improve stability.19:15 UTC on 26 June 2026 -Continuous monitoring and adjustments were performed to optimize resource distribution and support recovery22:40 UTC on 26 June 2026 - Service stability improved, with request success rates returning to expected levels. Customer impact was mitigated, and monitoring continued to validate full recovery. What happens next? This Mitigation Statement is the final communication for this incident. For details about which Azure incidents qualify for which Post Incident Reviews (PIRs), refer to https://aka.ms/AzurePIRs. The impact times above represent the full incident duration, so are not specific to any individual customer. Actual impact to service availability may vary between customers and resources – for guidance on implementing monitoring to understand granular impact: https://aka.ms/AzPIR/Monitoring To stay informed about future Azure service issues, make sure that you configure and maintain Azure Service Health alerts – these can trigger emails, SMS, push notifications, webhooks, and more: https://aka.ms/ash-alerts. For broader guidance on preparing for cloud incidents, refer to https://aka.ms/incidentreadiness.
